context:
Goal: several full test suites running at once stop slowing each other down.
Problem (rule): a fixed limit goes against your ruling of no fixed numbers (22 Oct, and 12:54 CST on 11 Nov), so the way the brake should count is your call.
Based on (read): the tile-windows session's report you forwarded: 3 to 5 suites at once turned a 9-minute run into 16 to 18 minutes (not re-read by triage).
Departs from: main — the load brake reads memory and disk only — it also refuses a new suite start while the machine reads busy.
Waiting on: nothing is stopped; the consultant builds step suite-load-brake on your answer.

options.how: The brake adds one reading at each suite start and refuses while it reads busy.
options.label: Refuse a new full-suite start while the machine reads busy (recommended)
options.lose: One more reading at every suite start.

options.how: The brake counts running suites and refuses a third.
options.label: A fixed limit of 2 suites
options.lose: Goes against your ruling of no fixed numbers.

ref: consultant message 15:23 CST Nov 18, from your 14:54 CST review list (feedback from the local tile-windows session)
reply: Closed on your pick c (15:46 CST, in the consultant's chat): no change to the load brake. Step suite-load-brake is set to dropped. The 9 to 18 minute slowdowns from parallel suites stay.

shown.label: Refuse a new full-suite start while the machine reads busy (recommended)

title: How should the machine's load brake stop several full test suites from slowing each other?
why: a follows your no-fixed-numbers ruling; b breaks it and c leaves the slowdown. Recommended by the consultant, not owner-typed.
